idiom_name: translation unit per table + sqlite3_stmt record-set loop
implementation_notes: C has neither classes nor a record-set type, so both halves are written by hand: one translation unit (table.h/table.c) per table exposing functions - or a struct of function pointers used as the module handle - and a result loop over sqlite3_prepare_v2(), sqlite3_step() and the sqlite3_column_*() family, which fills an array of row structs that acts as the Record Set. Prepare statements once and re-run them with sqlite3_reset() plus sqlite3_bind_*() when the same operation is applied to many parameter sets; there is no framework that will do the preparation, binding or lifetime management for you.
pitfalls: Every sqlite3_prepare_v2 must be paired with sqlite3_finalize; a missed finalize leaks the statement, and an unfinalized statement blocks schema changes and can keep the database locked.
Pointers returned by sqlite3_column_text()/column_blob() are invalidated by the next sqlite3_step(), reset or finalize - copy text and blobs into owned buffers before advancing.
